EARTHPULSE – NASA Earth System Trend Analyzer

Project Description

EARTHPULSE is an interactive climate data analysis and visualization platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. The project aims to improve the accessibility and understanding of historical climate information by transforming NASA datasets into meaningful visualizations and statistical insights. Its geographical focus is Kerala, India, with an emphasis on exploring regional temperature and precipitation patterns.

Functionality and Working

EARTHPULSE retrieves historical monthly climate data through the NASA POWER API. The primary parameters analyzed are T2M (temperature at 2 metres above the surface) and PRECTOTCORR (corrected precipitation).

The retrieved data is processed using Python-based data processing techniques and presented through an interactive Streamlit dashboard. Users can explore historical temperature variations, analyze monthly and yearly precipitation patterns, examine climate trends and compare supported geographical locations.

The platform incorporates statistical methods, including the Theil-Sen Estimator, Mann-Kendall Test and Kendall's Tau, to estimate trend magnitude, evaluate monotonic trend significance and understand the direction and strength of climate relationships.

Benefits and Intended Impact

EARTHPULSE simplifies the exploration of scientific climate datasets by presenting complex information through accessible visualizations and statistical analysis. It aims to support climate education, environmental awareness and exploratory research by helping users understand historical regional climate patterns.

The project also demonstrates the practical application of open NASA data in developing accessible environmental analysis tools.

Technology and Implementation

The application was developed using Python as its core programming language. Streamlit provides the interactive web interface, Pandas and NumPy support data processing and numerical computation, SciPy supports statistical analysis, and Plotly is used to generate interactive visualizations. NASA POWER API serves as the primary climate data source.

The project follows a modular software architecture that separates frontend components, backend data services, data processing and statistical analysis. No specialized hardware is required.

Creativity and Innovation

The primary innovation of EARTHPULSE lies in integrating NASA climate data retrieval, statistical trend detection and interactive visualization into a unified platform. Rather than requiring users to interpret raw scientific datasets independently, the application presents processed climate information in a more accessible and understandable format.

This approach provides an interactive way to investigate regional climate behaviour using publicly available Earth science data.

Development Considerations

During development, the team considered data reliability, scientific accuracy, usability, performance, accessibility and future scalability. Particular attention was given to selecting appropriate statistical techniques and interpreting results within the context of the selected location, observation period and available data.

Team Collaboration

EARTHPULSE was developed collaboratively by two team members.

Devu – Project Development and Integration: Primarily responsible for project implementation, frontend development, dashboard integration, project coordination, testing and debugging.

Sharon Binu George – Backend Development and Data Analysis: Primarily responsible for backend data services, NASA POWER API integration, climate data processing, statistical trend analysis and backend integration support.

Both members actively collaborated throughout the development, integration, testing and improvement processes.

Future Scope

Future development may include expanding geographical coverage, integrating additional Earth system variables, improving regional climate comparisons, introducing advanced analytical capabilities and enhancing geographical visualizations.

Conclusion

EARTHPULSE demonstrates how NASA climate data and modern software technologies can be combined to make historical climate information more accessible and understandable. By connecting data retrieval, scientific analysis and interactive visualization, the project aims to encourage greater awareness of regional climate patterns and support further exploration of Earth's changing environmental systems.

GitHub Repository: https://github.com/krizzdev7/Earthpulse
